PMID:41480472.topic: Tranexamic acid in hip fracture surgery
PMID:41480472.setting: Dorset County Hospital, Dorchester; district general hospital
PMID:41480472.standard: NICE guideline: offer TXA to adults having surgery expected to cause moderate blood loss (>500 ml)

cycle1.result: 26/37 (70.0%) eligible patients received intraoperative TXA; contraindication documented in 0%

PMID:41480472.intervention: Local hip fracture protocol updated to include TXA, targeted teaching for anaesthetic and theatre staff, and encouragement to record contraindications

cycle2.result: 23/27 (85.2%) received TXA; contraindication documented in 7.4%; difference not significant (Fisher's exact p = 0.23, OR 0.41)

PMID:41480472.other_findings: No thromboembolic complications in either cycle; transfusion and outcome data were not collected.

PMID:26734429.topic: Postoperative analgesia protocol compliance in arthroplasty
PMID:26734429.setting: Whittington Hospital, London; elective hip and knee arthroplasty in an enhanced recovery programme
PMID:26734429.standard: Local enhanced recovery multimodal postoperative analgesia protocol for elective hip and knee replacement

cycle1.dates: One week at the beginning of July 2014
cycle1.result: 0/27 patients received all medications according to the protocol

PMID:26734429.intervention: Electronic prescribing order set (JAC) for the analgesia protocol introduced in August 2014; results presented, re-education of rotating junior staff and protocol added to induction documentation

cycle2.result: Total compliance 58%; gabapentin 96%, modified-release morphine 96%, weak opioid 100%, conversion to PRN analgesia 100%, ibuprofen 58%

PMID:26734429.other_findings: Intermediate cycle in October 2014 (n=26) showed compliance of 34.6% (p<0.001); ibuprofen prescribing stayed poor, with 9/26 omitted without documented contraindication.

PMID:37767248.setting: Hull University Teaching Hospitals; emergency department and fracture clinic
PMID:37767248.standard: NICE guideline: manage paediatric distal radius buckle fractures with a soft cast and discharge directly from the ED

cycle1.result: 33/84 discharged at first visit; 69 had a single X-ray, 12 had two and 4 had three X-rays

PMID:37767248.intervention: Results presented to the department and ED; parents educated on fracture type and cast removal with option to forgo clinic visits; safety brochures; email reminders to fracture clinic staff about NICE guidance

cycle2.result: 62/64 discharged directly from the ED (42 focal rigidity cast removed at home, 10 backslab, 10 crepe bandage); 2 returned to plaster room and 1 to fracture clinic

PMID:37767248.other_findings: Extra visits, radiographs and cast changes in the first audit cost £18,078 over 6 months.

PMID:37333695.topic: Intrathecal fentanyl and postoperative opioid use after hip arthroplasty
PMID:37333695.setting: Complexo Hospitalario Universitario de A Coruña; primary total hip arthroplasty under spinal anaesthesia

cycle1.result: Mean PACU morphine use 4.76 mg (0 µg fentanyl, n=25), 4.39 mg (10 µg, n=255) and 7.33 mg (>10 µg, n=12), P=0.029; about 25% in each group needed opioids on the ward within 48 h

PMID:37333695.other_findings: Described as a clinical audit but is a retrospective association analysis without a standard.

PMID:40861770.topic: Virtual MDT decision time in acute arthroplasty
PMID:40861770.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust; tertiary referral centre for complex arthroplasty

cycle1.result: Mean time to decision via Siilo secure messaging 0.87 days versus conventional weekly MDT wait of 3.9 days; mean saving 3.03 days per case

PMID:40861770.other_findings: Commonest diagnoses were periprosthetic fracture (28), knee PJI (16) and dislocation (12); MDT wait was an estimated, not measured, comparator.

PMID:26734392.setting: Croydon University Hospital; planned orthopaedic trauma lists
PMID:26734392.standard: All intraoperative images available on PACS within 72 hours of being taken (local target)

cycle1.result: 9/27 (33%) images available within 72 hours; 4 (15%) delayed by failure to request, 14 (52%) requested but not processed

PMID:26734392.intervention: Radiographers told not to screen without a valid request; tick box added to trauma list submission template; agreement with radiology to upload within 72 hours; radiographers invited to trauma meeting; changes communicated by email and governance meetings

cycle2.dates: Two weeks, six weeks after the first post-intervention cycle
cycle2.result: 90% of images processed within 72 hours; delays from failure to request eliminated

PMID:26734392.other_findings: First post-intervention cycle (n=15) showed images not available fell from 66.0% to 13.3%.

PMID:39304219.setting: University Hospital Waterford; regional orthopaedic trauma service
PMID:39304219.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping standards (GSP 2014); target 80% or more for all aspects

cycle1.result: Poor documentation of 50% of aspects: author name 50%, date 70%, medications 20%, functional status 30%, investigation results 30%, social history 40%, systemic review 75%

PMID:39304219.intervention: Orthopaedic admission proforma introduced and discussed at morbidity and mortality meeting; then dedicated slots in departments and printable from any hospital computer

cycle2.result: Author name 100%, date 100%, medications 95%, social history 70%, functional status 65%, systemic review 90%, investigation results 35%

PMID:39304219.other_findings: Three cycles over 6 months (60 notes); investigation results stayed poor as results often not available at admission.

PMID:34103268.topic: COVID-19 impact on hip fracture services
PMID:34103268.setting: 185 units in 14 countries (national audits in Germany, Scotland and Ireland plus online survey)

cycle1.result: 102/160 (63.7%) units reported worse service quality; 74/160 (46.2%) had >50% reduction in theatre access; 135/160 (84.4%) reported reduced theatre efficiency

PMID:34103268.other_findings: Two thirds lost specialist orthopaedic nurses, a third lost orthogeriatric services and a quarter lost physiotherapists.

PMID:26734178.setting: Two district general hospitals without spinal units (London and KSS deaneries)
PMID:26734178.standard: Local standards of 95% for neurological examination, management plan, stability, permitted mobility and precautions documentation

cycle1.result: No criterion met the standard; hospital 1: neurological examination 74%, stability 44%, precautions 53%, permitted mobility 26%, delay in treatment 59%, serious medical concern 37% (7/19)

PMID:26734178.intervention: Spinal injuries proforma and ASIA chart placed on trust computers, introduced via M&M presentations, email and face-to-face; desktop icon added

cycle2.result: Hospital 1: neurological examination 100%, stability 95%, precautions 100%, permitted mobility 95%, delay in treatment 11%, serious medical concern 6% (1/18)

PMID:26734178.other_findings: Proforma used in 96% (hospital 1) and 100% (hospital 2) in first eight weeks; re-audit at hospital 2 ongoing.

PMID:26734354.topic: Hip fracture best practice tariff compliance
PMID:26734354.setting: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; acute hip fracture service
PMID:26734354.standard: National Hip Fracture Database best practice tariff criteria (surgery within 36 h, orthogeriatric review within 72 h, pre- and post-operative AMT, etc.)

cycle1.result: BPT achieved in 8/18 (44.4%); 4 waited >36 h for surgery, 7 >72 h for orthogeriatric review, 9 lacked both AMT scores; FI block in ED 3/18 (16.7%)

PMID:26734354.intervention: Eight-page multidisciplinary clerking booklet, hip fracture care group, twice-weekly consultant orthogeriatric ward rounds, and booklet in local induction

cycle2.result: BPT achieved in 22/24 (91.7%); all had both AMT scores; FI block in ED in 6

PMID:26734354.other_findings: Booklet used in 27/30 (90%) but ED section complete in only 20 (74.1%); mean acute stay fell from 18.9 to 16.4 days (p=0.066).

PMID:29326858.standard: NICE NG38: buckle fractures treated with non-rigid cast or splint without routine follow-up

cycle1.result: 59 fracture clinic visits; mean 1.9 visits per child

PMID:29326858.intervention: Parents taught about fracture type and soft cast removal and offered no further visits; information leaflet designed with plaster technicians and nurses
PMID:29326858.other_findings: Authors recommend implementing the guidance in A&E as well as fracture clinics.

PMID:32435926.topic: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
PMID:32435926.setting: 127 UK radiology departments (RCR national audit); 50 consecutive non-trauma CT studies each
PMID:32435926.standard: RCR audit standards: comment on vertebrae 100%, fracture severity, recommended terminology 'vertebral fracture' 100%, appropriate referral 100%

cycle1.result: 79% of reports commented on vertebrae; severity mentioned in 26.2%; recommended terminology in 60.1%; onward referral recommended in 2.6%

PMID:32435926.other_findings: 1362/6357 (21.4%) had a fracture on auditor review.

EPMC:PMC:PMC12260834.setting: Central Norfolk Older Adult Inpatient Unit, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
EPMC:PMC:PMC12260834.standard: NICE guidelines (2012): fracture risk assessment with FRAX or QFracture for women aged 65 and over

cycle1.result: 0% had documented FRAX/QFracture assessment or DEXA; only 19% on bone-protecting medication despite over 90% intermediate or high risk

EPMC:PMC:PMC12260834.other_findings: Described as a re-audit but earlier results are not reported; 60% had secondary risk factors and about 70% a history of falls.

PMID:41519655.topic: Surgical site infection prevention in hand and wrist trauma
PMID:41519655.setting: 45 hospitals in 12 countries via the Reconstructive Surgery Trials Network
PMID:41519655.standard: WHO global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection

cycle1.result: Surgical hand preparation 91%, drapes and gowns 92%, standard postoperative dressings 98%; adherence low for other antimicrobial practices

PMID:35396184.topic: AI detection of proximal femoral fractures
PMID:35396184.setting: Royal Adelaide Hospital; external validation at Stanford University Medical Center

cycle1.result: Model AUC 0.994 versus 0.969 for five radiologists; external validation AUC 0.980

PMID:35396184.other_findings: Algorithmic audit found an operating-point shift on external validation and more errors in abnormal bones such as Paget's disease.

PMID:31399208.topic: Clinician fracture detection on whole-body radiographs
PMID:31399208.setting: Two Level 1-equivalent public-sector trauma units, Cape Town

cycle1.result: Fracture detection rate 89% (95% CI 86–93%); 21 fractures missed, including all elbow fractures (3/3) and 9/13 shoulder girdle fractures

PMID:31399208.other_findings: One missed fracture clearly needed surgery and 7 others might have.

PMID:38944567.topic: VTE prophylaxis in foot and ankle surgery

cycle1.result: 3630 (31.95%) received no chemical anticoagulation; LMWH 6303 (84.4% of those treated), factor Xa inhibitor 10%, aspirin 4.1%; VTE 1.1% (83/7469) in those anticoagulated

PMID:38944567.other_findings: No significant difference in VTE between anticoagulant types; 6 weeks was the commonest duration (64.50%).

PMID:39463188.setting: Center of Orthopaedics and Traumatology, University Hospital Brandenburg/Havel; tertiary setting
PMID:39463188.standard: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for selection and administration of intra-articular knee injections

cycle1.result: Low adherence with all audit criteria, including informed patient decision-making and recommending alternative treatments

PMID:39463188.intervention: Educational briefings for physicians and informative flyers for patients

cycle2.result: Substantial improvements in several criteria, including stepwise referral to conservative therapy and injection content

PMID:39463188.other_findings: Numbers not given in the abstract.

PMID:32994070.topic: Malnutrition in overweight hip fracture patients
PMID:32994070.setting: Dedicated hip fracture unit, The Prince Charles Hospital, Brisbane

cycle1.result: Malnutrition prevalence 18.3%; 12-month mortality 17.3%; malnutrition increased odds of 12-month mortality (OR 4.47, p=0.020)

PMID:32994070.other_findings: Malnutrition also linked to delirium (OR 3.64) and delayed mobilisation (OR 3.29).

EPMC:PMC:PMC9378028.setting: Female later life psychiatry ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
EPMC:PMC:PMC9378028.standard: NICE and National Osteoporosis Guideline Group guidance on identification, assessment and management of fragility fracture risk

cycle1.result: FRAX calculated in 8/16 (50%) without known osteoporosis; FRAX communicated to GP in 2/8 (25%)

EPMC:PMC:PMC9378028.intervention: Fracture risk scoring added to structured ward round template and osteoporosis information posters displayed

cycle2.result: FRAX calculated in 15/17 (88%); FRAX communicated to GP in 11/15 (73%); BMD measured in 1/10 (10%) intermediate-risk patients

EPMC:PMC:PMC9378028.other_findings: None of the 4 high-risk patients were started on bisphosphonates.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8771450.setting: Broadmoor Hospital, high secure forensic psychiatry hospital, 15 wards
EPMC:PMC:PMC8771450.standard: Local trust guideline: vitamin D checked within one month of admission and then three-monthly, with dosing by level

cycle1.result: 76.4% checked within one month of admission; 66.7% checked in last 3 months; 21.4% correct dose, 22.9% under-dosed, 14.3% over-dosed, 41.4% no dose when indicated

EPMC:PMC:PMC8771450.other_findings: Deficiency fell from 43.6% at admission to 14.5% on most recent levels.

EPMC:PPR:PPR1267204.setting: Orthopaedic operating theatre, Regional Headquarter Hospital Skardu

cycle1.result: Scrub duration at least two minutes 45%, coverage of all surfaces 50%, proper antiseptic use 60%, correct drying 55%, overall aseptic protocol 70% (about 40 staff)

EPMC:PPR:PPR1267204.intervention: Live demonstrations of correct hand scrubbing and visual reminder posters in the scrub area

cycle2.result: Scrub duration 90%, coverage 88%, antiseptic use 93%, drying 87%, overall aseptic protocol 95%; all improvements statistically significant

PMID:32838821.setting: 140 Australian facilities contributing Surgical National Antimicrobial Prescribing Survey audits
PMID:32838821.standard: Surgical NAPS appropriateness assessment of surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Overall appropriateness 58.0% of 6709 doses; procedural 64.7%, postprocedural 48.3%

PMID:32838821.other_findings: Commonest reasons for inappropriateness were timing of procedural doses (50.9%) and duration of postprocedural prescriptions (49.8%).

PMID:25435737.setting: Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi; tertiary trauma centre
PMID:25435737.standard: College of American Pathologists guidelines for FFP transfusion

cycle1.result: Appropriate FFP use 49.5%

PMID:25435737.other_findings: Orthopaedics accounted for 12.6% of FFP use; neurosurgery had the highest appropriate use (50.5%).

PMID:25926312.setting: 61 NHS hospital trusts; colorectal, orthopaedic, urological and gynaecological surgery
PMID:25926312.standard: Enhanced Recovery protocol elements; good compliance defined as 80% or more

cycle1.result: Compliance weakly associated with shorter stay (r -0.18 colorectal, -0.14 orthopaedics, -0.25 gynaecology); 80% compliance linked to 2, 1 and 3 day shorter median stay in colorectal, orthopaedic and urological surgery

PMID:25926312.other_findings: No length of stay saving in gynaecology.

PMID:29727232.setting: Single centre; Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:29727232.standard: British Orthopaedic Association-endorsed consent guidance (12 potential risks)

cycle1.result: 4/12 risks documented in <50% of intracapsular fractures (n=35) and 7/12 in <50% of extracapsular fractures (n=35)

PMID:29727232.intervention: Raising awareness and attaching consent guidance; neck of femur fracture-specific consent form then implemented

cycle2.result: 100% documentation of potential risks in intracapsular and extracapsular fractures

EPMC:PMC:PMC9112772.setting: Multicentre quality improvement registry (16 institutions, 26 surgeons)

cycle1.result: Stiffness in 4.2%; surgery for stiffness in 1.1%; loss of extension 3.8%, loss of flexion 3.1%

EPMC:PMC:PMC9112772.other_findings: Stiffness linked to longer tourniquet time (93.0 vs 78.8 min) and anteriorly displaced meniscal tears.

PMID:33454063.setting: 3 major trauma centres and 5 trauma units
PMID:33454063.standard: BOA and BAPRAS standards for trauma (open fractures)

cycle1.result: Antibiotics within 1 hour 41.7%; splint in ED 74.4%; documented orthoplastic plan 85.8%; debridement within 12 hours for high-energy injuries 41.7%

PMID:33454063.other_findings: 42.3% of patients were managed at some point in a trauma unit.

PMID:11708425.setting: Repatriation General Hospital, Daw Park; tertiary teaching hospital

cycle1.dates: Hip fractures over 18 months and wrist fractures over 30 months
cycle1.result: 32% had BMD measured and 39% were offered osteoporosis treatment

PMID:11708425.other_findings: Only 34% received information from the medical profession; calcium alone made up 60% of treatments.

PMID:42517882.topic: Bisphosphonate exposure classification in atypical femur fractures
PMID:42517882.setting: Swedish population cohort and Kaiser Permanente Southern California cohort

cycle1.result: Sweden: no extra exposure found, 38/172 (22.1%) BP-naive; KPSC: prior BP use found in 20/29, BP-naive fell from 9.5% to 2.9%

PMID:41747609.setting: 22 hospitals in England, Wales and Scotland
PMID:41747609.standard: BOAST guideline for paediatric ACL injuries (2022)

cycle1.result: 65% of centres use acute knee pathways; 68% collaborative imaging pathways; 59% radiological growth monitoring; 30% report functional outcomes; <50% report re-rupture rates; 74% adhere to rehabilitation protocols

PMID:32115205.topic: Effect of hip fracture audit on outcomes
PMID:32115205.setting: Ten Dutch hospitals; Dutch Nationwide Trauma Registration

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation cohort; outcomes reported only as adjusted comparison with 2017

PMID:32115205.intervention: Implementation of the Dutch Hip Fracture Audit in 2017

cycle2.result: 30-day mortality adjusted OR 1.23 (95% CI 0.93–1.63); no difference in length of stay (-0.002) or time to surgery (0.292)

PMID:32115205.other_findings: Outcome comparison rather than audit against a standard.

PMID:26267012.topic: Hip fracture care against national standards
PMID:26267012.standard: UK Blue Book standards, compared with National Hip Fracture Database 2012 (180 UK hospitals)

cycle1.result: 66% admitted to orthopaedic ward within 24 h; 8% surgery within 48 h (UK 83%); 10% no surgery; 27% orthogeriatric assessment (UK 70%); 0.3% osteoporosis assessment (UK 94%); 3.8% falls assessment (UK 92%)

PMID:26267012.other_findings: New pressure ulcers in 2% versus 3.7% in the UK.

PMID:37994354.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
PMID:37994354.setting: North Manchester General Hospital; district general hospital

cycle1.result: ED: capillary refill 65%, radial pulse 59.2%, individual nerve function 37.9%; pre-op nerve function 42.7%; 2 mm K-wires 53.3%; post-op pulse/CRT 27.2%, nerve function 9.7%

PMID:37994354.intervention: Supracondylar fracture assessment proforma and focused educational sessions

cycle2.result: ED: capillary refill 95.5% (p=0.0038), radial pulse 95.5% (p=0.0009), nerve function 72.7% (p=0.0040); pre-op nerve function 50%; 2 mm K-wires 89.5%; post-op pulse/CRT 54.2%, nerve function 50%

PMID:37994354.other_findings: Medial wire technique documentation rose from 82.9% to 100% and post-fixation stability from 42.7% to 89.5%; pre-op nerve documentation stayed low.

PMID:26681169.topic: Fundamentals of nursing care in hip fracture
PMID:26681169.setting: University hospital in southern Sweden; national hip fracture quality register

cycle1.result: 28.5% walked outdoors at 4 months; about 30% still had pain and used analgesics at 4 months

PMID:26681169.other_findings: Length of stay and in-hospital complications fell between 2011 and 2013.

PMID:37652448.standard: Fragility Fracture Network minimum common dataset (2022): 20 core and 12 optional fields

cycle1.result: First-generation registries collect 60% of fields, second-generation 75%, third-generation 85%; 5/20 core fields collected by all; prefracture mobility, cognition and bone protection collected by 11/17 (65%)

PMID:39618239.setting: NHS hospitals in England; national collaborative audit with BOTA
PMID:39618239.standard: Completeness of NJR elbow dataset against Hospital Episode Statistics, and accuracy of recorded components

cycle1.result: Completeness 63%; radial head arthroplasty completeness 35%; accuracy 94%; 5539 unmatched and 448 inaccurate arthroplasties from 254 hospitals

PMID:39618239.intervention: National collaborative audit through trainees: hospitals checked records, added missing arthroplasties and corrected inaccurate ones

cycle2.result: Completeness 83% (total elbow arthroplasty 93%); radial head arthroplasty completeness 70%; accuracy 98% after correcting 212 of 448

PMID:39618239.other_findings: 82% of unmatched records were confirmed missing; radial head arthroplasties drove most of the gap.

EPMC:PMC:PMC10748749.topic: VTE prophylaxis in foot and ankle surgery

cycle1.result: 95 VTE events (0.86%); Achilles tendon rupture 3.7%; below-knee amputation 5.3%

EPMC:PMC:PMC10748749.other_findings: 12 different chemical prophylaxis agents used; no evidence mechanical prophylaxis reduced VTE.

PMID:32863141.topic: Ipsilateral shoulder pain after thoracic surgery

cycle1.result: Moderate-to-severe ipsilateral shoulder pain in 15.8% of thoracotomy patients; none in VATS patients given phrenic nerve infiltration

PMID:40523430.standard: Guidelines on daptomycin prescribing (appropriateness assessed by local referent)

cycle1.result: 87.1% (1128) appropriate; of 132 inappropriate prescriptions, 33.3% wrong indication, 25% no de-escalation, 16.7% wrong dose, 15.9% wrong duration

PMID:40523430.other_findings: 44.2% were for bone and joint infections; written infectious disease advice linked to higher appropriateness (94.1% vs 69.9%).
